tip: Trowch is a command with the -wch ending, used for a group or someone formal. To a single friend you'd say tro.
In reported speech, 'that' is carried by fod, a softened bod: Gwyddai hi fod y gwaith... = she knew that the work...
cei di is the future of cael, meaning you will get. So cei di ddirwy means you'll get a fine, not you already got one.
i'w gwblhau means to complete it: the 'w packs 'it' in before the verb, so the noun isn't repeated.
After the preposition o (of), the next word softens: cariad becomes gariad, giving symbol o gariad.
cael plus eu plus a verb makes a passive: cael eu gwnïo = are sewn. The eu points back to gwisgoedd, the costumes.
hon means this for feminine nouns. cymuned is feminine, so it's i'r gymuned hon. A masculine noun would take hwn.
mynd â means to take along: Es i â’r ci am dro = I took the dog for a walk, literally went with the dog.
Welsh has no word for of. llif yr afon = the flow of the river, literally flow the river, with yr on the last noun.
